Goal: demonstrate two isolated concurrent web-app-plus-Postgres development stacks on a consumer-owned local backend.
Keep the ordinary single-process CLI baseline free of required Docker or network infrastructure. For the multitier trial, use a documented process or container backend selected by the implementer. A named profile returning explicit app/database handles is only a proposal; evaluate that boundary without pretending it already exists.
Prove startup, correct app-to-database routing, separate workspaces/data, and no cross-stack access. Inject one startup failure and one cancellation; demonstrate bounded cleanup. Observe the useful progress and trouble in Gimbal's live UI, rather than treating a passing command as proof of legibility.
Budget: one local machine, at most two stacks; no hosted spend. Exclusions: Kubernetes deployment, universal restartability, automatic workflow-version migration, general compiler language expansion, and release/deployment gates. Produce an actionable sprint plan, not an implementation report.
